question: How many months does an African elephant's pregnancy last?
explainer: At about 22 months it is the longest gestation of any land mammal, nearly two and a half times a human pregnancy.

question: How many centimetres can the fastest-growing bamboo grow in a single day, per Guinness World Records?
source_title: Fastest growing plant - Guinness World Records
explainer: Some bamboo species shoot up 91 cm in 24 hours, nearly 4 cm every hour, so you can see the difference between breakfast and dinner.

question: How tall is Hyperion, the coast redwood in California that is the world's tallest known living tree, in metres?
explainer: At about 116 m Hyperion is taller than the Statue of Liberty including its pedestal (93 m); its exact location is kept secret to protect it.

question: How old was Jonathan, the Seychelles giant tortoise on St Helena and the oldest known living land animal, in 2025?
explainer: Jonathan is believed to have hatched around 1832, before the first photograph of a person was ever taken, and he is still grazing on the governor's lawn.

question: What is the fastest dive speed ever recorded for a peregrine falcon, in km/h?
explainer: At 389 km/h a stooping peregrine outpaces a Formula 1 car at full throttle, making it the fastest animal on Earth.

question: How many wild mountain gorillas were there in 2018, combining the latest Virunga and Bwindi census counts?
explainer: All of them live in just two forest regions of central Africa; the total combines the 2015-16 Virunga count (604) and the 2018 Bwindi-Sarambwe count (459), up from around 600 in the early 1980s.

question: How much does an average ostrich egg weigh, in grams?
explainer: At 1.4 kg a single ostrich egg holds about as much as two dozen chicken eggs and takes around an hour and a half to hard-boil.

question: What is the trunk volume of General Sherman, the giant sequoia in California that is the largest tree on Earth, in cubic metres?
explainer: About 1,487 cubic metres of wood in one trunk, enough to fill more than half an Olympic swimming pool.

question: What is the deepest dive ever recorded for a Cuvier's beaked whale, the deepest-diving mammal, in metres?
explainer: Nearly 3 km straight down, close to seven Empire State Buildings stacked end to end; the same species has also been logged holding its breath for more than three hours.

question: How old was Methuselah, the Great Basin bristlecone pine in California's White Mountains, in 2024?
explainer: It germinated around 2833 BC, before the Great Pyramid of Giza was built, and is still alive today.

question: How many tonnes of honey were produced worldwide in 2022, according to FAO?
explainer: Roughly 1.8 million tonnes a year, about 230 grams per person on Earth, with China by far the biggest producer.

question: How many living bird species were recognised on the IOC World Bird List as of 2024?
explainer: Around 11,000 species, roughly 6,500 of them passerines (perching birds), and a handful of new species are still described every year.

question: What is the longest non-stop flight recorded for a bird (a bar-tailed godwit tracked from Alaska to Tasmania in 2022), in km?
explainer: The five-month-old godwit flew 13,560 km in 11 days without stopping to eat, drink or rest, about a third of the way around the world.

question: How many spider species had been scientifically described worldwide, per the World Spider Catalog, as of 2024?
explainer: Over 52,000 named species, with hundreds more added every year; taxonomists suspect the true number may be double that.

question: What is the area of Australia's Great Barrier Reef, in square kilometres?
explainer: About 344,400 sq km, larger than Italy and visible from orbit, it is the biggest structure on Earth built by living things.

question: How many African elephants (savanna and forest) were estimated to remain in the wild in 2016, per the IUCN status report?
explainer: About 415,000, down from several million a century ago; Botswana alone is home to roughly a third of them.

question: How many tonnes did the world's wild-capture fisheries land in 2022, per FAO's State of World Fisheries report?
source_title: The State of World Fisheries and Aquaculture 2024 - FAO
explainer: About 92 million tonnes, and for the first time farmed seafood (aquaculture) now outproduces the wild catch.

question: How many eggs can a single female ocean sunfish carry at one time?
explainer: Up to 300 million eggs, more than any other known vertebrate, each only about a millimetre across.

question: How many yen did the top bluefin tuna fetch at Tokyo's first fish auction of 2019, a record price?
explainer: Sushi chain owner Kiyoshi Kimura paid 333.6 million yen (about US$3.1 million) for a 278 kg fish, over US$11,000 per kilogram.

question: How many hectares of forest did the world have in 2020, per the FAO Global Forest Resources Assessment?
explainer: 4.06 billion hectares, about 31% of all land, or roughly half a hectare of forest for every person alive.

question: How many chickens were slaughtered for meat worldwide in 2022?
source_title: Number of animals slaughtered for meat - Our World in Data
explainer: Around 75 billion, more than nine chickens per person on Earth every year, or about 200 million every single day.

question: How much did Americans spend on their pets in 2024, in US$, per the American Pet Products Association?
source_title: Industry Trends and Stats - American Pet Products Association
explainer: About $152 billion, or roughly $450 for every person in the United States, with food and treats the biggest slice of the bill.

question: How many trees are there on Earth, according to the 2015 global estimate published in Nature?
source_title: Mapping tree density at a global scale - Nature (Crowther et al. 2015)
explainer: About 3.04 trillion, roughly 400 trees per person, though the total has fallen by around 46% since the dawn of agriculture.

question: How many individual ants are estimated to live on Earth, per the 2022 study in PNAS?
source_title: The abundance, biomass, and distribution of ants on Earth - PNAS (Schultheiss et al. 2022)
explainer: About 20 quadrillion, 2.5 million ants for every human, and together they outweigh all wild birds and mammals combined.
